name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q01 - Vitamin content increase in curd formation

questiontext.text: The vitamin whose content increases following the conversion of milk into curd by lactic acid bacteria is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Lactic acid bacteria (LAB), such as Lactobacillus, grow in milk and convert lactose sugar into lactic acid. The produced acid coagulates and partially digests milk proteins, transforming milk into curd.

Step 2: Nutritional Enrichment
In addition to transforming milk texture and checking disease-causing microbes in the stomach, the metabolic activity of lactic acid bacteria significantly improves the nutritional quality of curd by synthesizing and enhancing the concentration of vitamin B12.

Step 3: Conclusion
Thus, the vitamin whose content increases during curd formation by lactic acid bacteria is vitamin B12.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q02 - Treatment of sludge in wastewater treatment

questiontext.text: Wastewater treatment generates a large quantity of sludge, which can be treated by:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Sludge Generation in Sewage Treatment
During sewage treatment, substantial quantities of solids are separated as primary sludge and secondary activated sludge.

Step 2: Processing in Anaerobic Digesters
A small part of the activated sludge is recycled back into the aeration tank to serve as an inoculum. The major remaining portion is pumped into large, closed tanks called anaerobic sludge digesters. In these digesters, anaerobic microbes digest the biomass of aerobic bacteria and fungi, breaking down organic solids and generating biogas.

Step 3: Conclusion
Therefore, the large quantity of sludge produced during wastewater treatment is treated by anaerobic digesters.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q03 - Occurrence of methanogenic bacteria in habitats

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Environmental Requirements of Methanogens
Methanogens, such as Methanobacterium, are obligate anaerobes that require strictly oxygen-free conditions to thrive and ferment cellulosic compounds. They naturally colonize the anaerobic rumen of ruminants, flooded soils at the bottom of water-logged paddy fields, and the anaerobic digesters of biogas (gobar gas) plants.

Step 2: Nature of Activated Sludge
Activated sludge forms in the aeration tank during secondary treatment, where constant agitation and mechanical pumping supply abundant oxygen to support aerobic bacterial and fungal flocs. Because this environment is continuously oxygenated, obligate anaerobic methanogenic bacteria cannot survive or grow in it.

Step 3: Conclusion
Hence, methanogenic bacteria are not found in activated sludge.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q04 - Commercial bacterial products and their sources

questiontext.text:
Match the following list of bacteria and their commercially important products:

Bacterium Product
A. Aspergillus niger i. Lactic acid
B. Acetobacter aceti ii. Butyric acid
C. Clostridium butylicum iii. Acetic acid
D. Lactobacillus iv. Citric acid

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Industrial Microorganisms and Organic Acids
Specific microorganisms are utilized for the large-scale commercial production of organic acids:

  • Aspergillus niger (a fungus) is used industrially to synthesize citric acid.
  • Acetobacter aceti (a bacterium) oxidizes ethanol to produce acetic acid.
  • Clostridium butylicum (a bacterium) ferments carbohydrates to produce butyric acid.
  • Lactobacillus (a bacterium) produces lactic acid during lactose/glucose fermentation.

Step 2: Conclusion
The correct match pairs Aspergillus niger with citric acid, Acetobacter aceti with acetic acid, Clostridium butylicum with butyric acid, and Lactobacillus with lactic acid (A-iv, B-iii, C-ii, D-i).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q05 - Bioactive substances and their biological roles

questiontext.text:
Match the following list of bioactive substances and their roles:

Bioactive Substance Role
A. Statin i. Removal of oil stains
B. Cyclosporin A ii. Removal of clots from blood vessels
C. Streptokinase iii. Lowering of blood cholesterol
D. Lipase iv. Immuno-suppressive agent

Choose the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Bioactive Molecules and Their Applications
Microbially produced bioactive molecules carry distinct therapeutic and practical functions:

  • Statin: Derived from the yeast Monascus purpureus, statins competitively inhibit the rate-limiting enzyme in cholesterol biosynthesis and serve to lower blood cholesterol.
  • Cyclosporin A: Obtained from the fungus Trichoderma polysporum, this cyclic peptide acts as an immunosuppressive agent in organ-transplant recipients.
  • Streptokinase: Produced by the bacterium Streptococcus, it functions as a 'clot buster' to dissolve intravascular thrombi from blood vessels of patients suffering myocardial infarction.
  • Lipase: Secreted by various microbes, lipid-digesting enzymes are incorporated into detergent formulations for the removal of greasy oil stains from textiles.

Step 2: Conclusion
Thus, statin matches with lowering of blood cholesterol, cyclosporin A matches with immuno-suppressive agent, streptokinase matches with removal of clots from blood vessels, and lipase matches with removal of oil stains (A-iii, B-iv, C-ii, D-i).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q06 - Removal process during primary wastewater treatment

questiontext.text: The primary treatment of waste water involves the removal of:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Mechanism of Primary Treatment
Primary sewage treatment is a purely physical process designed to separate solid particulate matter through sequential filtration and sedimentation. Coarse floating debris is intercepted by mesh screens, followed by primary settling basins where stable, suspended settleable particles such as grit (soil, sand, and pebbles) settle out by gravity.

Step 2: Processing of Non-Physical Impurities
Dissolved organic pollutants, toxic compounds, and pathogenic microorganisms are not removed by primary physical settling; rather, dissolved biological waste is decomposed in secondary biological treatment, and disinfection targets microorganisms during tertiary treatment.

Step 3: Conclusion
Hence, primary treatment of wastewater focuses on the removal of stable particles.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q07 - Estimation of biological oxygen demand wastewater

questiontext.text: BOD of waste water is estimated by measuring the amount of:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Definition of BOD
Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) denotes the quantity of dissolved oxygen required by aerobic microbes to oxidize all the biodegradable organic matter contained in one liter of wastewater.

Step 2: Measurement Principle
Although BOD serves as an indirect gauge of the total biodegradable organic load, the assay experimentally quantifies the rate and total magnitude of dissolved oxygen consumption by the microbial population during aerobic breakdown.

Step 3: Conclusion
Consequently, BOD of wastewater is estimated by measuring the amount of oxygen consumption.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q08 - Alcoholic beverage produced without using distillation

questiontext.text: Which one of the following alcoholic drinks is produced without distillation?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Production Pathways of Alcoholic Drinks
Fermented beverages are categorized into undistilled and distilled products depending on whether the fermented mash undergoes downstream concentration via thermal distillation.

Step 2: Comparison of Beverages
Wine and beer are produced by natural yeast fermentation without subsequent distillation, yielding moderate alcohol percentages. In contrast, whisky, rum, and brandy are prepared by distilling fermented broths to achieve significantly higher alcohol contents.

Step 3: Conclusion
Therefore, among the beverages listed, wine is produced without distillation.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q09 - Development of biogas production technology India

questiontext.text: The technology of biogas production from cow dung was developed in India largely due to the efforts of:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Historical Role of Indian Research Bodies
The practical engineering and microbiological design of anaerobic digesters for harnessing biogas (gobar gas) from livestock waste in rural India was spearheaded by specialized agricultural and rural industrial bodies.

Step 2: Contribution of IARI and KVIC
The Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) and the Khadi & Village Industries Commission (KVIC) formulated standardized biogas plant designs that enabled widespread adoption of rural bio-energy generation across India.

Step 3: Conclusion
Thus, biogas technology development from cow dung in India is credited to the Indian Agricultural Research Institute and Khadi & Village Industries Commission.

answer.text: Indian Agricultural Research Institute and Khadi & Village Industries Commission

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q10 - Free living fungus used biocontrol agent

questiontext.text: The free-living fungus Trichoderma can be used for:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Biology of Trichoderma
Trichoderma is a free-living, soil-dwelling ascomycete fungus that commonly populates the rhizosphere and root surfaces of higher plants.

Step 2: Biocontrol Mechanism
It acts as an effective biocontrol agent against a broad spectrum of phytopathogenic fungi through niche competition, mycoparasitism, and secretion of cell-wall lytic enzymes, safeguarding crops from soil-borne diseases.

Step 3: Conclusion
Therefore, the free-living fungus Trichoderma is used for biological control of plant diseases.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q11 - Effect of reduced oxygen on flocs

questiontext.text: What would happen if oxygen availability to activated sludge flocs is reduced?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Structural Organization of Flocs
Activated sludge flocs consist of tight associations of aerobic bacteria intertwined with fungal hyphae. Maintaining a high concentration of dissolved oxygen is essential to ensure oxygen diffuses into the deep internal regions of these aggregates.

Step 2: Impact of Oxygen Depletion
When the dissolved oxygen supply is restricted, the core of the flocs becomes depleted of oxygen (anoxic). Under anoxia, obligate aerobic bacteria inside the core die and lyse, leading to the disintegration and breakage of the flocs, which ruins their settleability and degrades treatment efficacy.

Step 3: Conclusion
Hence, reducing oxygen availability causes the center of flocs to become anoxic, causing death of bacteria and eventual breakage of flocs.

answer.text: It will slow down the rate of degradation of organic matter
The center of flocs will become anoxic, which would cause death of bacteria and eventually breakage of flocs.
Flocs would increase in size as anaerobic bacteria would grow around flocs.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q12 - Role of mycorrhiza in host plant

questiontext.text: Mycorrhiza does not help the host plant in:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Benefits of Mycorrhizal Associations
Mycorrhizae represent mutualistic associations between fungi (e.g., Glomus) and the root systems of host plants. The fungal partner absorbs essential minerals, especially phosphorus, from the soil and transfers them to the plant. It also confers resistance against root-borne pathogens and increases plant tolerance to abiotic stresses such as salinity and drought.

Step 2: Target Scope of Protection
Mycorrhizal symbiosis does not provide protection or resistance against insect pests; resistance to insects relies on plant morphological traits, secondary metabolites, or entomopathogenic biocontrol agents.

Step 3: Conclusion
Therefore, mycorrhiza does not help the host plant in increasing its resistance to insects.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q13 - Organism that does not fix nitrogen

questiontext.text: Which one of the following is not a nitrogen-fixing organism?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Nitrogen-Fixing Microorganisms
Diazotrophic organisms possess nitrogenase enzyme complexes that convert atmospheric dinitrogen (\(\text{N}_2\)) into biological ammonia. Well-known nitrogen fixers include cyanobacteria such as Anabaena and Nostoc, as well as free-living soil bacteria such as Azotobacter.

Step 2: Ecological Function of Pseudomonas
Pseudomonas species do not fix atmospheric nitrogen; instead, they function primarily as denitrifying bacteria in the nitrogen cycle, transforming soil nitrates (\(\text{NO}_3^-\)) and nitrites (\(\text{NO}_2^-\)) into dinitrogen gas (\(\text{N}_2\)).

Step 3: Conclusion
Thus, Pseudomonas is not a nitrogen-fixing organism.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q14 - Formation of large holes in cheese

questiontext.text: Big holes in Swiss cheese are made by a:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Production and Ripening of Swiss Cheese
The characteristic large holes (often referred to as 'eyes') in Swiss cheese are formed during fermentation and ripening.

Step 2: Microbial Agent Involved
These holes develop due to the metabolic activity of the bacterium Propionibacterium sharmanii, which produces large amounts of carbon dioxide (\(\text{CO}_2\)) as a byproduct of propionic acid fermentation. As gas bubbles expand within the curd, they form distinct hollow cavities.

Step 3: Conclusion
Therefore, big holes in Swiss cheese are made by a bacterium producing a large amount of carbon dioxide.

answer.text: a bacterium producing a large amount of carbon dioxide
a fungus that releases a lot of gases during its metabolic activities.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q15 - Utilization of cattle dung biogas residue

questiontext.text: The residue left after methane production from cattle dung is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Generation of Digested Slurry
In an agricultural biogas digester, cattle dung is mixed with water and subjected to anaerobic digestion by methanogens to generate methane-rich fuel gas.

Step 2: Agricultural Value of Spent Residue
The slurry that overflows from the digestion chamber retains virtually all of the nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and humic components of the dung without foul odors or pathogen load, making it exceptionally valuable as nutrient-dense organic manure for crop soils.

Step 3: Conclusion
Hence, the spent residue remaining after biogas generation from cattle dung is used as manure.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q16 - Gaseous products not formed by methanogens

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Physiology of Methanogenic Bacteria
Methanogens (such as Methanobacterium) are obligate anaerobes that live under strictly reduced, oxygen-free conditions.

Step 2: Gaseous Byproducts of Methanogenesis
During the anaerobic decomposition of cellulosic biomass, methanogens produce biogas consisting mainly of methane (\(\text{CH}_4\)) and carbon dioxide (\(\text{CO}_2\)), along with traces of hydrogen sulfide (\(\text{H}_2\text{S}\)). Because methanogens are obligate anaerobes to which oxygen is lethal, they do not produce oxygen.

Step 3: Conclusion
Therefore, methanogens do not produce oxygen.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q17 - Rapid settling ability of activated sludge

questiontext.text: Activated sludge should have the ability to settle quickly so that it can:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Role of Settling in Secondary Treatment
Once biological aeration drastically lowers wastewater BOD, the liquid enters a secondary settling tank where the microbial flocs settle under gravity to form activated sludge.

Step 2: Sludge Recirculation Purpose
Rapid settling is required to cleanly separate the treated effluent from the biomass, allowing an aliquot of the settled microbial flocs to be promptly pumped back into the aeration tank to maintain a high inoculum of active aerobic microorganisms for the next cycle.

Step 3: Conclusion
Thus, activated sludge must possess the capability to settle rapidly so that it can be rapidly pumped back from the sedimentation tank to the aeration tank.

answer.text: be rapidly pumped back from sedimentation tank to aeration tank
absorb pathogenic bacteria present in waste water while sinking to the bottom of the settling tank

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q18 - Biological agents and their corresponding functions

questiontext.text:
Match the items in Column 'A' and Column 'B' and choose correct answer.

Column I Column II
A. Lady bird i. Methano bacterium
B. Mycorrhiza ii. Trichoderma
C. Biological control iii. Aphids
D. Biogas iv. Glomus

The correct answer is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of Pairs
Each biological agent or phenomenon pairs with its specific ecological partner or application:

  • Lady bird: The ladybird beetle is a predatory insect employed as a biocontrol agent against agricultural aphid infestations.
  • Mycorrhiza: Symbiotic mycorrhizal root associations are formed prominently by members of the fungal genus Glomus.
  • Biological control: The free-living fungus Trichoderma serves as an effective biological control agent against numerous crop-pathogenic fungi.
  • Biogas: Production of methane-rich biogas is carried out by methanogenic archaebacteria such as Methanobacterium.

Step 2: Conclusion
Consequently, Lady bird corresponds to aphids, Mycorrhiza to Glomus, Biological control to Trichoderma, and Biogas to Methanobacterium (A-iii, B-iv, C-ii, D-i).
